namespace HopfEntanglement

open Complex

/-! ## The Hopf map -/

/-- The Hopf map `ℂ² → ℂ × ℝ`, `h(z, w) = (2 z w̄, |z|² - |w|²)`. -/
def hopf (z w : ℂ) : ℂ × ℝ := (2 * z * (starRingEnd ℂ) w, Complex.normSq z - Complex.normSq w)

/-- **The Hopf map lands on spheres.**  `‖h(z,w)‖² = (|z|² + |w|²)²`; in particular
`h` maps the unit `3`-sphere `|z|² + |w|² = 1` into the unit `2`-sphere. -/
theorem hopf_norm_sq (z w : ℂ) :
    Complex.normSq (hopf z w).1 + ((hopf z w).2) ^ 2
      = (Complex.normSq z + Complex.normSq w) ^ 2 := by
  simp only [hopf, map_mul, Complex.normSq_conj]
  have h2 : Complex.normSq 2 = 4 := by simp; norm_num
  rw [h2]
  ring

/-- **The Hopf map sends the 3-sphere to the 2-sphere.** -/
theorem hopf_maps_sphere (z w : ℂ) (h : Complex.normSq z + Complex.normSq w = 1) :
    Complex.normSq (hopf z w).1 + ((hopf z w).2) ^ 2 = 1 := by
  rw [hopf_norm_sq, h]; norm_num

/-- **The fibres are circles.**  The Hopf map is invariant under the diagonal action
of the unit circle. -/
theorem hopf_phase_invariant (z w u : ℂ) (hu : Complex.normSq u = 1) :
    hopf (u * z) (u * w) = hopf z w := by
  have hconj : u * (starRingEnd ℂ) u = 1 := by
    rw [Complex.mul_conj]
    exact_mod_cast congrArg (fun r : ℝ => (r : ℂ)) hu
  refine Prod.ext ?_ ?_
  · show 2 * (u * z) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (u * w) = 2 * z * (starRingEnd ℂ) w
    rw [map_mul]
    calc 2 * (u * z) * ((starRingEnd ℂ) u * (starRingEnd ℂ) w)
        = (u * (starRingEnd ℂ) u) * (2 * z * (starRingEnd ℂ) w) := by ring
      _ = 2 * z * (starRingEnd ℂ) w := by rw [hconj, one_mul]
  · show Complex.normSq (u * z) - Complex.normSq (u * w)
        = Complex.normSq z - Complex.normSq w
    rw [Complex.normSq_mul, Complex.normSq_mul, hu, one_mul, one_mul]

/-- The Hopf map is *exactly* constant on circles: the third coordinate detects the
north/south poles. -/
theorem hopf_pole_iff (z w : ℂ) (h : Complex.normSq z + Complex.normSq w = 1) :
    (hopf z w).2 = 1 ↔ w = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro hz
    have hw : Complex.normSq w = 0 := by
      simp only [hopf] at hz
      have : Complex.normSq z = 1 + Complex.normSq w := by linarith
      linarith [this, h]

# Neural Hodge theory: definitions

This module previously contained only a stray relative path pointing at a
non-existent file `Shared/NeuralHodge/Defs.lean`.  It is reconstructed here as the
definitional layer of a discrete Hodge/Laplacian theory on a finite weighted graph

is the architecture of a network and the Laplacian is its smoothing operator.

* `NeuralHodge.Weights` — a finite symmetric non-negative weight system with zero
  diagonal (an undirected weighted graph on `Fin n`);
* `NeuralHodge.degree`, `NeuralHodge.laplacian`, `NeuralHodge.energy`,
  `NeuralHodge.dot` — degree, graph Laplacian, Dirichlet energy and inner product;

  `laplacian_smul`) and kills constants (`laplacian_const`), and the harmonic
  (Hodge) space contains the constants.

namespace NeuralHodge

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A finite undirected weighted graph on the vertex set `Fin n`. -/
structure Weights (n : ℕ) where
  /-- the weight of the edge `{i, j}` -/
  w : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ
  /-- weights are symmetric -/
  w_symm : ∀ i j, w i j = w j i
  /-- weights are non-negative -/
  w_nonneg : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ w i j
  /-- there are no self-loops -/
  w_diag : ∀ i, w i i = 0

/-- The (weighted) degree of a vertex. -/
def degree (W : Weights n) (i : Fin n) : ℝ := ∑ j, W.w i j

/-- The graph Laplacian `L x i = deg(i) · x i − ∑ⱼ w i j · x j`. -/
def laplacian (W : Weights n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  degree W i * x i - ∑ j, W.w i j * x j

/-- The Dirichlet energy `E(x) = ½ ∑ᵢⱼ w i j (x i − x j)²`. -/
noncomputable def energy (W : Weights n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / 2) * ∑ i, ∑ j, W.w i j * (x i - x j) ^ 2

/-- The Euclidean inner product on vertex functions. -/
def dot (x y : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i, x i * y i

/-- A vertex function is **harmonic** (a discrete Hodge class) when the Laplacian
annihilates it. -/
def IsHarmonic (W : Weights n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop := ∀ i, laplacian W x i = 0

/-! ## Elementary properties -/

theorem degree_nonneg (W : Weights n) (i : Fin n) : 0 ≤ degree W i :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun j _ => W.w_nonneg i j

theorem laplacian_add (W : Weights n) (x y : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) :
    laplacian W (fun k => x k + y k) i = laplacian W x i + laplacian W y i := by
  simp only [laplacian, mul_add]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  ring

theorem laplacian_smul (W : Weights n) (c : ℝ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) :
    laplacian W (fun k => c * x k) i = c * laplacian W x i := by
  unfold laplacian
  have h : ∑ j, W.w i j * (c * x j) = c * ∑ j, W.w i j * x j := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => by ring
  rw [h]
  ring

/-- **Constants are harmonic.**  The Laplacian kills constant functions, so the
harmonic space is non-trivial whenever `n > 0`. -/
theorem laplacian_const (W : Weights n) (c : ℝ) (i : Fin n) :
    laplacian W (fun _ => c) i = 0 := by
  simp only [laplacian, degree, ← Finset.sum_mul]
  ring

theorem isHarmonic_const (W : Weights n) (c : ℝ) : IsHarmonic W (fun _ => c) :=
  fun i => laplacian_const W c i

@[simp] theorem energy_const (W : Weights n) (c : ℝ) : energy W (fun _ => c) = 0 := by
  simp [energy]

end NeuralHodge

    by_contra hcon

  intro k hk hp

    have : (n + 1)! + 2 + k = (n + 1)! + (k + 2) := by omega
    rw [this]

  Nat.sInf_le ⟨hN, hp⟩

    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ : ∃ k, q = m + k := ⟨q - m, by omega⟩

    by_contra hcon

theorem tropSum_le {s : Finset ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → ℝ) {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) :
    tropSum s hs f ≤ f i := Finset.inf'_le f hi

theorem le_tropSum {s : Finset ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → ℝ) {c : ℝ}
    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, c ≤ f i) : c ≤ tropSum s hs f := Finset.le_inf' hs f h

theorem exists_ground_state {s : Finset ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → ℝ) :
    ∃ i ∈ s, tropSum s hs f = f i := by
  obtain ⟨i, hi, hval⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' hs f
  exact ⟨i, hi, hval⟩

/-- **Energy shift.**  Adding a constant to every energy shifts the ground state
energy by the same constant — tropical multiplication by a scalar. -/
theorem tropSum_shift {s : Finset ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → ℝ) (c : ℝ) :
    tropSum s hs (fun i => f i + c) = tropSum s hs f + c := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · obtain ⟨i, hi, hval⟩ := exists_ground_state hs f
    calc tropSum s hs (fun i => f i + c) ≤ f i + c := tropSum_le hs _ hi
      _ = tropSum s hs f + c := by rw [hval]
  · refine le_tropSum hs _ fun i hi => ?_
    linarith [tropSum_le hs f hi]

/-- **Factorization over products.**  The ground state energy of a system whose
energy is a sum of independent contributions is the sum of the ground state
energies.  This is the tropical analogue of `Z(A ⊗ B) = Z(A) · Z(B)`. -/
theorem tropSum_product {s : Finset ι} {t : Finset κ} (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty)
    (f : ι → ℝ) (g : κ → ℝ) :
    tropSum (s ×ˢ t) (hs.product ht) (fun p => f p.1 + g p.2)
      = tropSum s hs f + tropSum t ht g := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · obtain ⟨i, hi, hfi⟩ := exists_ground_state hs f
    obtain ⟨j, hj, hgj⟩ := exists_ground_state ht g
    have hmem : (i, j) ∈ s ×ˢ t := Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hi, hj⟩
    calc tropSum (s ×ˢ t) (hs.product ht) (fun p => f p.1 + g p.2)
        ≤ f i + g j := tropSum_le (hs.product ht) _ hmem
      _ = tropSum s hs f + tropSum t ht g := by rw [hfi, hgj]
  · refine le_tropSum (hs.product ht) _ fun p hp => ?_
    obtain ⟨hp1, hp2⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hp
    exact add_le_add (tropSum_le hs f hp1) (tropSum_le ht g hp2)

/-- **Extensivity.**  Two independent identical subsystems have exactly twice the
ground state energy of one. -/
theorem tropSum_square {s : Finset ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → ℝ) :
    tropSum (s ×ˢ s) (hs.product hs) (fun p => f p.1 + f p.2) = 2 * tropSum s hs f := by
  rw [tropSum_product hs hs f f]
  ring

/-- **Monotonicity.**  A larger configuration space has a lower (or equal) ground
state energy. -/
theorem tropSum_antitone {s t : Finset ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty)
    (hst : s ⊆ t) (f : ι → ℝ) : tropSum t ht f ≤ tropSum s hs f := by
  refine le_tropSum hs f fun i hi => tropSum_le ht f (hst hi)

/-- **The tropical Fubini law.**  Minimizing over a product can be done in either
order. -/
theorem tropSum_comm {s : Finset ι} {t : Finset κ} (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty)
    (F : ι → κ → ℝ) :
    tropSum s hs (fun i => tropSum t ht (fun j => F i j))
      = tropSum t ht (fun j => tropSum s hs (fun i => F i j)) := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · refine le_tropSum ht _ fun j hj => ?_
    refine le_tropSum hs _ fun i hi => ?_
    exact le_trans (tropSum_le hs _ hi) (tropSum_le ht _ hj)
  · refine le_tropSum hs _ fun i hi => ?_
    refine le_tropSum ht _ fun j hj => ?_
    exact le_trans (tropSum_le ht _ hj) (tropSum_le hs _ hi)

end TropicalEntropy

import Shared.TropicalentropyDefs.TropicalEntropy_Defs

/-!
# Tropical spectral graph theory

This module previously contained only a stray relative path pointing at a
non-existent file `Shared/TropicalSpectralGraph/Theorems.lean`.  It is
reconstructed here as a self-contained development of **min-plus (tropical) matrix
algebra** on a finite complete weighted digraph, the algebraic backbone of tropical
spectral graph theory: tropical matrix powers compute shortest walks, and the
tropical eigenvalue is a minimal cycle mean.

Main results:

* `TropicalGraph.mpMul` — the min-plus matrix product, together with
  `TropicalGraph.mpMul_assoc` (**associativity**, i.e. the Bellman optimality
  principle) and `TropicalGraph.mpMul_one` / `one_mpMul` (the tropical identity);
* `TropicalGraph.mpMul_le` — the shortest-walk upper bound `(A ⊗ B) i j ≤ A i k + B k j`;
* `TropicalGraph.mpMul_mono` — monotonicity in both arguments;
* `TropicalGraph.mpMul_shift` — the **spectral shift**: adding a constant `c` to all
  entries shifts every tropical eigenvalue by `c`;
* `TropicalGraph.mpPow_add` and `TropicalGraph.mpPow_le_mul` — the concatenation
  law for tropical powers, the input to Fekete's lemma for the minimal cycle mean.
-/

namespace TropicalGraph

open Finset TropicalEntropy

variable {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]

/-- The index set is non-empty, so `inf'` is available. -/
private lemma univ_ne : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).Nonempty :=
  Finset.univ_nonempty (α := Fin n)

/-- A weighted digraph: `A i j` is the length of the arc `i → j`. -/
abbrev Weighting (n : ℕ) : Type := Fin n → Fin n → ℝ

/-- **Min-plus matrix product.**  `(A ⊗ B) i j = min_k (A i k + B k j)`. -/
noncomputable def mpMul (A B : Weighting n) : Weighting n :=
  fun i j => tropSum Finset.univ univ_ne (fun k => A i k + B k j)

/-- The defining upper bound: every intermediate vertex gives an upper bound. -/
theorem mpMul_le (A B : Weighting n) (i j k : Fin n) : mpMul A B i j ≤ A i k + B k j :=
  tropSum_le univ_ne _ (Finset.mem_univ k)

/-- The defining lower bound. -/
theorem le_mpMul (A B : Weighting n) (i j : Fin n) {c : ℝ}
    (h : ∀ k, c ≤ A i k + B k j) : c ≤ mpMul A B i j :=
  le_tropSum univ_ne _ fun k _ => h k

/-- The minimum is attained. -/
theorem exists_mpMul_eq (A B : Weighting n) (i j : Fin n) :
    ∃ k, mpMul A B i j = A i k + B k j := by
  obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := exists_ground_state univ_ne (fun k => A i k + B k j)
  exact ⟨k, hk⟩

/-- **Associativity (Bellman's optimality principle).**  Splitting an optimal walk
at any point gives optimal sub-walks. -/
theorem mpMul_assoc (A B C : Weighting n) : mpMul (mpMul A B) C = mpMul A (mpMul B C) := by
  funext i j
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · refine le_mpMul _ _ _ _ fun l => ?_
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_mpMul_eq B C l j
    calc mpMul (mpMul A B) C i j ≤ mpMul A B i k + C k j := mpMul_le _ _ i j k
      _ ≤ (A i l + B l k) + C k j := by
          have := mpMul_le A B i k l
          linarith
      _ = A i l + (B l k + C k j) := by ring
      _ = A i l + mpMul B C l j := by rw [hk]
  · refine le_mpMul _ _ _ _ fun k => ?_
    obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := exists_mpMul_eq A B i k
    calc mpMul A (mpMul B C) i j ≤ A i l + mpMul B C l j := mpMul_le _ _ i j l
      _ ≤ A i l + (B l k + C k j) := by
          have := mpMul_le B C l j k
          linarith
      _ = (A i l + B l k) + C k j := by ring
      _ = mpMul A B i k + C k j := by rw [hl]

/-- The tropical identity matrix: `0` on the diagonal, `+∞` off it — modelled here
by a sufficiently large finite penalty is not needed, since we state the identity
laws against an explicit bound. -/
noncomputable def tropOne (M : ℝ) : Weighting n := fun i j => if i = j then 0 else M

/-- With a penalty `M` at least as large as the spread of `A`, the tropical identity
is a left unit. -/
theorem one_mpMul (A : Weighting n) (M : ℝ)
    (hM : ∀ i j k : Fin n, A i j ≤ M + A k j) :
    mpMul (tropOne M) A = A := by
  funext i j
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · have := mpMul_le (tropOne M) A i j i
    simpa [tropOne] using this
  · refine le_mpMul _ _ _ _ fun k => ?_
    by_cases hk : i = k
    · subst hk
      simp [tropOne]
    · simp only [tropOne, if_neg hk]
      exact hM i j k

/-- With the same hypothesis the tropical identity is a right unit. -/
theorem mpMul_one (A : Weighting n) (M : ℝ)
    (hM : ∀ i j k : Fin n, A i j ≤ A i k + M) :
    mpMul A (tropOne M) = A := by
  funext i j
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · have := mpMul_le A (tropOne M) i j j
    simpa [tropOne] using this
  · refine le_mpMul _ _ _ _ fun k => ?_
    by_cases hk : k = j
    · subst hk
      simp [tropOne]
    · simp only [tropOne, if_neg hk]
      exact hM i j k

/-- **Monotonicity.**  The min-plus product is monotone in both arguments. -/
theorem mpMul_mono {A A' B B' : Weighting n}
    (hA : ∀ i j, A i j ≤ A' i j) (hB : ∀ i j, B i j ≤ B' i j) (i j : Fin n) :
    mpMul A B i j ≤ mpMul A' B' i j := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_mpMul_eq A' B' i j
  calc mpMul A B i j ≤ A i k + B k j := mpMul_le _ _ i j k
    _ ≤ A' i k + B' k j := add_le_add (hA i k) (hB k j)
    _ = mpMul A' B' i j := hk.symm

/-- **Spectral shift.**  Adding the constant `c` to every arc weight of `A` and `d`
to every arc weight of `B` shifts every entry of the product by `c + d`; in
particular every tropical eigenvalue of `A` shifts by `c`. -/
theorem mpMul_shift (A B : Weighting n) (c d : ℝ) (i j : Fin n) :
    mpMul (fun i j => A i j + c) (fun i j => B i j + d) i j = mpMul A B i j + (c + d) := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := exists_mpMul_eq A B i j
    have h : mpMul (fun i j => A i j + c) (fun i j => B i j + d) i j
        ≤ (A i k + c) + (B k j + d) := mpMul_le _ _ i j k
    rw [hk]
    linarith
  · refine le_mpMul _ _ _ _ fun k => ?_
    have h := mpMul_le A B i j k
    show mpMul A B i j + (c + d) ≤ (A i k + c) + (B k j + d)
    linarith

/-- Tropical powers: `mpPow A m` is the matrix of shortest walks using exactly
`m + 1` arcs. -/
noncomputable def mpPow (A : Weighting n) : ℕ → Weighting n
  | 0 => A
  | m + 1 => mpMul A (mpPow A m)

@[simp] lemma mpPow_zero (A : Weighting n) : mpPow A 0 = A := rfl

lemma mpPow_succ (A : Weighting n) (m : ℕ) : mpPow A (m + 1) = mpMul A (mpPow A m) := rfl

/-- **Concatenation of shortest walks.**  Optimal walks of lengths `p + 1` and
`q + 1` concatenate to the optimal walk of length `p + q + 2`: the shortest-walk
matrices multiply tropically.  This is the exact (rather than merely
sub-multiplicative) form of the hypothesis of Fekete's lemma that produces the
minimal cycle mean, i.e. the tropical spectral radius. -/
theorem mpPow_add (A : Weighting n) (p q : ℕ) :
    mpPow A (p + q + 1) = mpMul (mpPow A p) (mpPow A q) := by
  induction p with
  | zero =>
      rw [show 0 + q + 1 = q + 1 by omega, mpPow_succ, mpPow_zero]
  | succ m ih =>
      have hidx : m + 1 + q + 1 = (m + q + 1) + 1 := by omega
      rw [hidx, mpPow_succ, ih, mpPow_succ, mpMul_assoc]

/-- Consequently the tropical powers are sub-additive entrywise. -/
theorem mpPow_le_mul (A : Weighting n) (p q : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) :
    mpPow A (p + q + 1) i j ≤ mpMul (mpPow A p) (mpPow A q) i j := by
  rw [mpPow_add]

end TropicalGraph

# Computational evidence — anti-gravity statistics on small libraries

All numbers below are produced by `Catalog/Shared/AntiGravityExperiments.lean`
(`#eval`, exhaustive enumeration, no sampling). A *library* here is a finite set of
theorems with a dependency relation; on three theorems there are `2^9 = 512` of them,
encoded by a 9-bit code `m` (bit `3i+j` = "theorem `i` depends on theorem `j`").

## 1. Exhaustive enumeration on three theorems

| measured quantity | value |
|---|---|
| acyclic libraries (labelled DAGs on 3 nodes) | **25** |
| libraries whose heavy class (`weight ≥ 1`) is support-cofinal | **343** |
| **acyclic** libraries whose heavy class is support-cofinal | **0** |
| acyclic libraries whose heavy class is foundation-cofinal (dual notion) | **18** |
| libraries where direct weight *decreases* along a dependency edge | **237** |
| libraries where transitive influence decreases along a dependency edge | **0** |

## 2. OEIS

The count of acyclic libraries on `n` labelled theorems is the number of labelled
DAGs, **OEIS A003024**: `1, 1, 3, 25, 543, 29281, …`. Our enumeration reproduces the
term `25` for `n = 3`.

## 3. What the numbers say about the conjectures

* **Support-cofinality (= topological density of the anti-gravity class) is common
  among arbitrary relations (343/512 = 67%) but impossible once the library is
  acyclic (0/25).** This is the finite shadow of the proved theorem
  `AntiGravityDensity.not_dense_antiGravity_of_acyclic`: the obstruction is a terminal
  theorem, which every finite acyclic library has and whose weight is `0`. Since real
  formal libraries are acyclic, the unconditional "10% are anti-gravity, densely"
  prediction is refuted for every one of them, not merely for the edgeless example of
  the previous cycle.
* **The dual reading survives (18/25 = 72% of acyclic libraries).** Foundation-cofinality
  — every theorem is *built on* a heavy theorem — is compatible with acyclicity, which is
  why `AntiGravityDensity.antiGravity_dense_foundation` is a non-vacuous repair.
* **Direct weight is fragile (237/512 libraries order two dependency-comparable theorems
  the "wrong" way), transitive influence never is (0/512).** This is the finite shadow of
  `AntiGravityInfluence.influence_antitone` and motivated proving the separation example
  `AntiGravityInfluence.influence_separates_weight` on four theorems, where
  `weight 0 = 1 < 2 = weight 1` while `influence 1 = 3 < 4 = influence 0`.

## 4. Counterexample hunt

The universal claim "in every library, a positive fraction of theorems is anti-gravity
and that class is dense" was tested against all 512 three-theorem libraries. Among the
25 acyclic ones the claim fails **every single time**, and the failure is uniform: the
witness is always a terminal theorem. This is what suggested — and is now subsumed by —
the general theorem `not_dense_antiGravity_of_acyclic`.

The quantitative (counting) form of the claim, by contrast, is attainable: the family
`AntiGravityDensity.hubLib n` of acyclic libraries on `10n` theorems has exactly `n`
anti-gravity theorems for every `n` (`hubLib_density`), i.e. exactly ten percent, while
still failing topological density (`hubLib_counting_vs_topology`).

# Future directions — anti-gravity mathematics, cycle 1

This cycle proved (all `sorry`-free, in `Catalog/Shared/AntiGravityInfluence.lean` and
`Catalog/Shared/AntiGravityDensity.lean`):

* **Acyclicity obstruction.** In every finite, nonempty, *acyclic* library the
  anti-gravity theorems are never dense in the Alexandrov dependency topology
  (`not_dense_antiGravity_of_acyclic`), and more precisely a class is dense iff it
  contains every terminal theorem (`dense_iff_terminals_subset`); the terminal
  (weight-`0`) theorems form the *least* dense class (`terminals_isLeast_dense`).
* **Soundness is a separation axiom.** For a library with no self-invocation, the
  dependency topology is `T0` iff the library is acyclic (`t0_iff_acyclic`), so `T0`
  libraries never have dense anti-gravity classes (`t0_excludes_antiGravity_density`).
* **The dual repair.** Passing to the opposite library turns support into grounding;
  sources are cofinal downwards (`sources_dense_foundation`), and if every source is
  heavy and short then the anti-gravity theorems *are* dense in the foundation topology
  (`antiGravity_dense_foundation`).
* **Refactoring invariance.** The wrapper refactoring preserves the whole support
  preorder (`wrap_supports_some_iff`, `wrap_supports_none_iff`) while collapsing the
  direct weight of the wrapped theorem to `1` (`wrap_weight_target_lt`); transitive
  influence changes by at most one (`wrap_influence_close`). Influence is also monotone
  along dependency (`influence_antitone`), which direct weight is not
  (`influence_separates_weight`).
* **A structural ten-percent criterion.** A Markov inequality for the weight
  distribution plus the handshake identity give `ten_percent_of_bounded_reuse`: if no
  theorem is used by more than twenty others but the average reuse is at least three,
  then at least a tenth of the theorems are used at least twice — no charging map
  needed. The hypotheses are satisfiable by an acyclic library (`linLib_ten_percent`).
* **Quantitative side.** The charging certificate bound for an arbitrary ratio `k`
  (`card_le_mul_card_of_charging`), its sharpness at `k = 10`
  (`starLib_ten_percent_sharp`), and an increasing family with anti-gravity density
  exactly `1/10` at every size (`hubLib_density`) that is nevertheless never dense
  (`hubLib_counting_vs_topology`).

Four bold, testable conjectures come out of this.

## Conjecture 1 (Cofinality gap). *A `T0` library admits an anti-gravity class of counting density `1/k` only if it has at least `card/k` sources.*

Formally: for a finite acyclic library, if `charge : α → α` is a `k`-bounded charging
map onto theorems of weight `≥ w0`, then the number of *sources* is at least
`card α / (k · (w0 + 1))`.

**The key insight is** that acyclicity forces the heavy theorems to sit strictly below
the terminal layer, so a bounded charging map is a bounded-degree flow from the leaves to
the foundations, and flow conservation converts the counting density into a lower bound
on the number of foundational lemmas.

**Why now?** The `k`-bounded charging theorem and the source/terminal duality are both
already formalized here, so the conjecture is one flow-counting lemma away, and it turns
the empirical "10%" folklore into a *prediction about how many axioms a library needs*,
which can be measured directly on `Mathlib`.

## Conjecture 2 (Refactoring rigidity). *Transitive influence is the unique weight statistic, up to additive constants, that is invariant under wrapper insertion and monotone along dependency.*

Formally: let `μ` assign a natural number to each theorem of each finite library, be
monotone along `Supports`, and satisfy `|μ(wrap L t)(some x) − μ(L)(x)| ≤ C` for all
wrapper refactorings. Conjecture: `μ` is determined by the cone of `x` — it factors
through `cone L x` — and if `μ` is additive over disjoint unions of libraries then
`μ = a · influence + b`.

**The key insight is** that repeated wrapper insertions generate enough of the
refactoring groupoid to force any bounded-perturbation statistic to be a function of the
support preorder alone, and additivity then pins it to a cone count.

**Why now?** `wrap_supports_some_iff` shows the support preorder is exactly the invariant
part of a wrapper refactoring, and `wrap_influence_close` shows influence realizes the
bound `C = 1`; what remains is a rigidity argument, not a new definition.

## Conjecture 3 (Layered growth). *Under "bounded fan-in, unbounded reuse" growth, the fraction of theorems of weight `≥ w0` converges to a positive limit determined only by the fan-in distribution.*

Formally: let `L n` be an increasing family with in-degrees bounded by `d` and every
theorem used at least once until the last layer. Conjecture: the lower density of
`{x | weight ≥ w0}` is at least `1/(d(w0+1))`, and the hub family `hubLib` is extremal.

**The key insight is** that the handshake identity forces `Σ weight = Σ in-degree ≤ d·n`,
so a positive fraction of theorems must be heavy unless the weight distribution is
concentrated — and concentration is exactly what a bounded charging certificate forbids.

**Why now?** `hubLib_density` supplies the extremal family with exact density `1/10`,
`card_le_mul_card_of_charging` supplies the converse direction, and
`ten_percent_of_bounded_reuse` already proves the special case `d = 20`, `w0 = 2`,
average reuse `3`; the missing step is a distributional argument over layers that turns
the fixed constants into the general fan-in bound.

## Conjecture 4 (Topological dichotomy for real libraries). *For every finite library, exactly one of: the dependency topology is `T0`, or some anti-gravity class is dense — and the second case forces a dependency cycle through every theorem.*

Formally: if `{x | IsAntiGravity L w0 l0 x}` is dense for some `w0 ≥ 1`, then every
theorem supports a theorem lying on a cycle.

**The key insight is** that `t0_iff_acyclic` identifies the separation axiom with
soundness, so density of a positive-weight class is not a statistic about a library but a
certificate of circular reasoning — the topological statement and the logical statement

# Future Directions: Reflective Type Theory

## 1. Positivity as the exact semantic frontier

**Conjecture.** A reflective fixed-point code admits a monotone interpretation in every complete Heyting algebra if and only if each occurrence of its bound variable has positive variance. Moreover, failure of positivity is witnessed by a two-element algebra.

The key insight is that the same variance discipline governing recursive types also governs Knaster–Tarski semantics for self-referential provability. **Why now?** The syntax–semantics boundary is explicit: unrestricted codes have been separated from the guarded fragment, making both directions of the criterion testable.

## 2. Minimal-frame classification of uniterated provability

**Conjecture.** Up to bounded morphism, every finite pointed model satisfying `□P ∧ ¬□□P` contains the pointed two-edge chain as a generated quotient; in particular, three worlds are minimal when seriality is imposed at the distinguished world and its successor.

The key insight is that failure of axiom 4 must expose a composable pair of accessibility edges whose composite edge is absent. **Why now?** An explicit minimal witness and the universal transitivity obstruction provide the two extremal cases needed for a structural classification.

## 3. Conservative embedding of dependent type theory

**Conjecture.** Adding positive reflective fixed points to an intensional dependent type theory with normalization preserves canonicity for closed natural-number terms and is conservative over judgments not containing reflection or fixed points.

The key insight is to stratify reduction so that ordinary dependent computation cannot inspect reflective evidence, while guarded unfolding remains productive. **Why now?** The syntactic proper-extension theorem isolates the new constructors; the next test is whether their operational rules preserve the metatheory of the embedded fragment.

## 4. Alternation depth versus reflection depth

**Conjecture.** On finite transitive converse-well-founded frames, modal fixed-point alternation depth is bounded above by reflective proof depth plus frame height, and this bound is asymptotically sharp.

The key insight is that transitivity collapses repeated boxes while fixed-point alternation consumes ordinal rank. **Why now?** The frame boundary for iterated provability and the exact grammar translation make both complexity measures simultaneously available.

## 5. Diagonal incompleteness from internal fixed points

**Conjecture.** Every sound reflective theory able to represent substitution and a guarded negative fixed point contains a closed proposition that is true and unprovable, without postulating an external diagonal operator.

The key insight is that the diagonal sentence should be synthesized from the fixed-point constructor itself once substitution is representable. **Why now?** The external diagonal theorem establishes the logical endpoint, while the modal fixed-point grammar identifies the missing internal construction precisely.

-- NEW_FILE: Catalog/Logic/GuardedFixedPointUniqueness.lean
/-
# Guarded Operators on Converse Well-Founded Frames Have Unique Fixed Points

The positivity analysis (`ReflectiveFixedPointPositivity.lean`) shows that
*positive* reflective codes are solvable in every complete Heyting algebra by
Knaster–Tarski, while negative ones — such as `¬X` — need not be solvable at
all.  The diagonal analysis (`InternalDiagonalFixedPoint.lean`) shows that the
*guarded* negative equation `G ↔ ¬□G` nevertheless has a unique solution on the
canonical `GL` frame.

This file explains both phenomena by a single theorem, which uses **no
monotonicity whatsoever**:

> On a converse well-founded frame, every **guarded** operator on the powerset
> frame has exactly one fixed point.

Here an operator `F : Set W → Set W` is *guarded* when membership of `w` in
`F S` depends only on the restriction of `S` to the strict `R`-successors of
`w`.  Existence is by well-founded recursion, uniqueness by well-founded
induction.

Main results:

* `Guarded` — the guardedness (contractivity) condition.
* `guarded_exists_fixed_point`, `guarded_unique_fixed_point`,
  `guarded_existsUnique_fixed_point` — the theorem.
* `guarded_box`, `guarded_compl`, `guarded_inter`, `guarded_union`,
  `guarded_const`, `guarded_box_comp` — a closure calculus, so that guardedness
  can be read off syntactically from any code in which the bound variable occurs
  only under `□`.
* `gl_negated_box_unique`, `gl_nested_unique` — corollaries on the canonical
  `GL` frame `(ℕ, >)`: the Gödel equation `X = ¬□X` and the nested equation
  `X = ¬□¬□X` each have exactly one solution, *irrespective of the variance of
  the bound variable*.
* `succFrame_two_solutions` — converse well-foundedness is **necessary**: on the
  successor frame on `ℕ`, which is serial but has infinite ascending chains, the
  guarded equation `X = ¬□X` has at least two solutions (the even and the odd
  numbers).  So the uniqueness above is a genuine well-foundedness phenomenon,
  not a formality.
-/

import Mathlib

namespace GuardedFixedPoint

variable {W : Type*}

/-- `w ∈ boxOf R S` iff every `R`-successor of `w` lies in `S`. -/
def boxOf (R : W → W → Prop) (S : Set W) : Set W := {w | ∀ v, R w v → v ∈ S}

@[simp] lemma mem_boxOf (R : W → W → Prop) (S : Set W) (w : W) :
    w ∈ boxOf R S ↔ ∀ v, R w v → v ∈ S := Iff.rfl

/-- An operator on the powerset frame is *guarded* (contractive) when membership
of `w` in `F S` only depends on `S` at the strict `R`-successors of `w`. -/
def Guarded (R : W → W → Prop) (F : Set W → Set W) : Prop :=
  ∀ (S T : Set W) (w : W), (∀ v, R w v → (v ∈ S ↔ v ∈ T)) → (w ∈ F S ↔ w ∈ F T)

/-! ## The closure calculus for guardedness -/

theorem guarded_const (R : W → W → Prop) (A : Set W) :
    Guarded R (fun _ => A) := fun _ _ _ _ => Iff.rfl

theorem guarded_box (R : W → W → Prop) : Guarded R (boxOf R) := by
  intro S T w h
  simp only [mem_boxOf]
  exact ⟨fun hs v hv => (h v hv).1 (hs v hv), fun ht v hv => (h v hv).2 (ht v hv)⟩

theorem guarded_compl {R : W → W → Prop} {F : Set W → Set W} (hF : Guarded R F) :
    Guarded R (fun S => (F S)ᶜ) := by
  intro S T w h
  simpa using not_congr (hF S T w h)

theorem guarded_inter {R : W → W → Prop} {F G : Set W → Set W}
    (hF : Guarded R F) (hG : Guarded R G) : Guarded R (fun S => F S ∩ G S) := by
  intro S T w h
  exact and_congr (hF S T w h) (hG S T w h)

theorem guarded_union {R : W → W → Prop} {F G : Set W → Set W}
    (hF : Guarded R F) (hG : Guarded R G) : Guarded R (fun S => F S ∪ G S) := by
  intro S T w h
  exact or_congr (hF S T w h) (hG S T w h)

/-- On a transitive frame, boxing a guarded operator keeps it guarded; this is
what makes *nested* modalities guarded. -/
theorem guarded_box_comp {R : W → W → Prop} (htrans : Transitive R)
    {F : Set W → Set W} (hF : Guarded R F) :
    Guarded R (fun S => boxOf R (F S)) := by
  intro S T w h
  simp only [mem_boxOf]
  constructor
  · intro hs v hv
    refine (hF S T v ?_).1 (hs v hv)
    intro u hu
    exact h u (htrans hv hu)
  · intro ht v hv
    refine (hF S T v ?_).2 (ht v hv)
    intro u hu
    exact h u (htrans hv hu)

/-! ## Existence and uniqueness -/

/-- The set produced by well-founded recursion along the converse of `R`. -/
noncomputable def guardedFun (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hwf : WellFounded (fun a b => R b a)) (F : Set W → Set W) : W → Prop :=
  hwf.fix (C := fun _ => Prop) (fun w ih => w ∈ F {v | ∃ h : R w v, ih v h})

/-- The set produced by well-founded recursion along the converse of `R`. -/
noncomputable def guardedFix (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hwf : WellFounded (fun a b => R b a)) (F : Set W → Set W) : Set W :=
  {w | guardedFun R hwf F w}

private lemma guardedFix_spec (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hwf : WellFounded (fun a b => R b a)) (F : Set W → Set W) (w : W) :
    (w ∈ guardedFix R hwf F) ↔
      w ∈ F {v | ∃ _ : R w v, v ∈ guardedFix R hwf F} := by
  show guardedFun R hwf F w ↔ _
  unfold guardedFun
  rw [WellFounded.fix_eq]
  exact Iff.rfl

/-- **Existence.** A guarded operator on a converse well-founded frame has a
fixed point. -/
theorem guarded_exists_fixed_point (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hwf : WellFounded (fun a b => R b a)) {F : Set W → Set W}
    (hF : Guarded R F) : F (guardedFix R hwf F) = guardedFix R hwf F := by
  ext w
  rw [guardedFix_spec R hwf F w]
  refine hF (guardedFix R hwf F) {v | ∃ _ : R w v, v ∈ guardedFix R hwf F} w ?_
  intro v hv
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  constructor
  · intro hvS
    exact ⟨hv, hvS⟩
  · rintro ⟨-, hvS⟩
    exact hvS

/-- **Uniqueness.** Two fixed points of a guarded operator on a converse
well-founded frame coincide. -/
theorem guarded_unique_fixed_point (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hwf : WellFounded (fun a b => R b a)) {F : Set W → Set W}
    (hF : Guarded R F) {S T : Set W} (hS : F S = S) (hT : F T = T) : S = T := by
  ext w
  induction w using hwf.induction with
  | _ w ih =>
      have hagree : ∀ v, R w v → (v ∈ S ↔ v ∈ T) := fun v hv => ih v hv
      calc w ∈ S ↔ w ∈ F S := by rw [hS]
        _ ↔ w ∈ F T := hF S T w hagree
        _ ↔ w ∈ T := by rw [hT]

/-- **Guarded fixed-point theorem.**  On a converse well-founded frame every
guarded operator — positive, negative or of mixed variance — has exactly one
fixed point. -/
theorem guarded_existsUnique_fixed_point (R : W → W → Prop)
    (hwf : WellFounded (fun a b => R b a)) {F : Set W → Set W}
    (hF : Guarded R F) : ∃! S : Set W, F S = S := by
  refine ⟨guardedFix R hwf F, guarded_exists_fixed_point R hwf hF, ?_⟩
  intro T hT
  exact guarded_unique_fixed_point R hwf hF hT (guarded_exists_fixed_point R hwf hF)

/-! ## Corollaries on the canonical `GL` frame `(ℕ, >)` -/

/-- The canonical `GL` accessibility relation on `ℕ`: `R n m` iff `m < n`. -/
def glR : ℕ → ℕ → Prop := fun n m => m < n

theorem glR_converse_wf : WellFounded (fun a b => glR b a) := by
  simpa [glR] using (wellFounded_lt : WellFounded (· < · : ℕ → ℕ → Prop))

theorem glR_transitive : Transitive glR := fun _ _ _ hab hbc => lt_trans hbc hab

/-- **The Gödel equation has exactly one solution.**  `X = ¬□X` is a *negative*
equation, so Knaster–Tarski does not apply, yet guardedness gives existence and
uniqueness. -/
theorem gl_negated_box_unique : ∃! S : Set ℕ, (boxOf glR S)ᶜ = S :=
  guarded_existsUnique_fixed_point glR glR_converse_wf
    (guarded_compl (guarded_box glR))

/-- **The positive guarded equation has exactly one solution** as well: `X = □X`
(semantic Löb, recovered from the same theorem). -/
theorem gl_box_unique : ∃! S : Set ℕ, boxOf glR S = S :=
  guarded_existsUnique_fixed_point glR glR_converse_wf (guarded_box glR)

/-- Its solution is `univ`. -/
theorem gl_box_solution : boxOf glR (Set.univ : Set ℕ) = Set.univ := by
  ext n
  simp [boxOf]

/-- **A nested mixed-variance equation has exactly one solution.**
`X = ¬□¬□X` mixes two negations under two modalities; transitivity of the frame
keeps it guarded. -/
theorem gl_nested_unique : ∃! S : Set ℕ, (boxOf glR (boxOf glR S)ᶜ)ᶜ = S :=
  guarded_existsUnique_fixed_point glR glR_converse_wf
    (guarded_compl (guarded_box_comp glR_transitive (guarded_compl (guarded_box glR))))

/-! ## Converse well-foundedness is necessary

The successor frame on `ℕ` is serial and guarded equations still make sense on
it, but uniqueness fails: `X = ¬□X` has (at least) the two parity solutions. -/

/-- The successor frame: `R n m` iff `m = n + 1`.  It has infinite ascending
chains, so it is not converse well-founded. -/
def succR : ℕ → ℕ → Prop := fun n m => m = n + 1

theorem succR_not_converse_wf : ¬ WellFounded (fun a b => succR b a) := by
  intro hwf
  obtain ⟨n, _, hmin⟩ := hwf.has_min Set.univ ⟨0, trivial⟩
  exact hmin (n + 1) trivial rfl

theorem evens_fixed : (boxOf succR {n : ℕ | n % 2 = 0})ᶜ = {n : ℕ | n % 2 = 0} := by
  ext n
  simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, mem_boxOf, Set.mem_setOf_eq, succR, not_forall]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, hne⟩
    subst hv
    omega
  · intro hn
    exact ⟨n + 1, rfl, by omega⟩

theorem odds_fixed : (boxOf succR {n : ℕ | n % 2 = 1})ᶜ = {n : ℕ | n % 2 = 1} := by
  ext n
  simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, mem_boxOf, Set.mem_setOf_eq, succR, not_forall]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, hne⟩
    subst hv
    omega
  · intro hn
    exact ⟨n + 1, rfl, by omega⟩

frame the guarded Gödel equation has two distinct solutions. -/

    ∃ S T : Set ℕ, S ≠ T ∧ (boxOf succR S)ᶜ = S ∧ (boxOf succR T)ᶜ = T := by

  have : (0 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | n % 2 = 1} := h ▸ (by simp : (0 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | n % 2 = 0})

well-foundedness hypothesis distinguishes the two corollaries above. -/
theorem succR_negbox_guarded : Guarded succR (fun S => (boxOf succR S)ᶜ) :=
  guarded_compl (guarded_box succR)

# Internal Diagonalization: Guarded Negative Fixed Points

This file addresses the conjecture

> *Every sound reflective theory able to represent substitution and a guarded
> negative fixed point contains a closed proposition that is true and
> unprovable, without postulating an external diagonal operator.*

and, at the same time, sharpens the positivity analysis of
`ReflectiveFixedPointPositivity`: there, the *unguarded* negative code `¬X` was
shown to have **no** fixed point in the two-element Heyting algebra.  Here we
show that putting the variable under a **converse well-founded modality**
restores solvability: the guarded negative equation `G ↔ ¬□G` has a solution in
the powerset frame of the canonical `GL` frame `(ℕ, >)`, and the solution is
**unique**.  So the true semantic frontier for solvability is not positivity but
*positivity-or-guardedness*.

Main results:

* `godelSet_diagonal` — the set `G = {n | 1 ≤ n}` satisfies `n ∈ G ↔ n ∉ □G`
  at every world: a semantic Gödel sentence obtained without any external
  diagonal operator, purely as a fixed point of a negative code.
* `godel_fixed_point_unique` — **uniqueness** of that fixed point (a de Jongh /
  Sambin style uniqueness phenomenon).
* `unguarded_negation_no_fixed_point` — the contrast: without the `□` guard the
  same equation `p ↔ ¬p` has no solution at all.
* `boxGL_unique_fixed_point` — semantic Löb: the *positive* guarded equation
  `X ↔ □X` has the single solution `univ`, so the whole gap between the two
  regimes is created by the sign, not by the guard.
* `godel_true_but_unprovable` — at world `1` the Gödel set holds while `□G`
  fails: truth without provability.
* `ReflectiveTheory`, `godel_sentence_true_and_unprovable` — an abstract
  packaging: any sound reflective theory possessing an internal guarded negative
  fixed point has a true unprovable sentence.  Two instances are provided, one
  showing the axioms are consistent (`trivialTheory`) and one showing the
  diagonal clause is realised by the `GL` semantics (`glDiagonalTheory`),
  together with `pointwise_soundness_fails`, which explains exactly why the
  soundness clause has to be external.
-/

import Mathlib

namespace InternalDiagonal

/-! ## The canonical `GL` frame and its box operator -/

/-- The `□` operator of the canonical `GL` frame `(ℕ, >)`: `n ∈ □S` iff every
`m < n` lies in `S`.  The frame is transitive and converse well-founded. -/
def boxGL : Set ℕ →o Set ℕ where
  toFun := fun S => {n | ∀ m, m < n → m ∈ S}
  monotone' := by
    intro S T hST n hn m hm
    exact hST (hn m hm)

@[simp] lemma mem_boxGL (S : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    n ∈ boxGL S ↔ ∀ m, m < n → m ∈ S := Iff.rfl

/-- `0` satisfies every boxed statement: it is the `GL`-endpoint. -/
lemma zero_mem_boxGL (S : Set ℕ) : 0 ∈ boxGL S := by
  intro m hm
  exact absurd hm (Nat.not_lt_zero m)

/-! ## Semantic Löb: the positive guarded equation has a unique solution -/

/-- **Semantic Löb.**  The positive guarded equation `X = □X` has `univ` as its
unique solution on the canonical `GL` frame. -/
theorem boxGL_unique_fixed_point (S : Set ℕ) (hS : boxGL S = S) : S = Set.univ := by
  ext n
  simp only [Set.mem_univ, iff_true]
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
      have : n ∈ boxGL S := fun m hm => ih m hm
      rwa [hS] at this

/-- Consequently `univ` is the only fixed point, and in particular the least
fixed point of `□` is `univ`. -/
theorem lfp_boxGL : OrderHom.lfp boxGL = Set.univ :=
  boxGL_unique_fixed_point _ (OrderHom.map_lfp boxGL)

/-! ## The guarded *negative* equation: an internal Gödel sentence -/

/-- The semantic Gödel sentence: "not provable", i.e. all worlds of positive
rank. -/
def godelSet : Set ℕ := {n | 1 ≤ n}

/-- **Internal diagonalization.**  `godelSet` solves the guarded negative
equation `G ↔ ¬□G` at every world, with no external diagonal operator: it is a
fixed point of the negative code `X ↦ ¬□X`. -/
theorem godelSet_diagonal (n : ℕ) : n ∈ godelSet ↔ n ∉ boxGL godelSet := by
  constructor
  · intro hn hbox
    have h0 : (0 : ℕ) ∈ godelSet := hbox 0 (by simpa [godelSet] using hn)
    simp [godelSet] at h0
  · intro hn
    by_contra hng
    apply hn
    intro m hm
    simp only [godelSet, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hng ⊢
    omega

/-- Equivalently, as an equation of sets. -/
theorem godelSet_eq_compl_box : godelSet = (boxGL godelSet)ᶜ := by
  ext n
  simpa using godelSet_diagonal n

/-- **Uniqueness of the internal Gödel sentence.**  Any solution of
`T ↔ ¬□T` equals `godelSet`. -/
theorem godel_fixed_point_unique (T : Set ℕ)
    (hT : ∀ n, n ∈ T ↔ n ∉ boxGL T) : T = godelSet := by
  have h0 : (0 : ℕ) ∉ T := by
    intro h
    exact ((hT 0).1 h) (zero_mem_boxGL T)
  ext n
  constructor
  · intro hn
    simp only [godelSet, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hpos
    · exact absurd hn h0
    · exact hpos
  · intro hn
    have hpos : 0 < n := by simpa [godelSet] using hn
    refine (hT n).2 ?_
    intro hbox
    exact h0 (hbox 0 hpos)

/-- **Truth without provability.**  At world `1` the Gödel sentence holds while
`□G` fails. -/
theorem godel_true_but_unprovable : (1 : ℕ) ∈ godelSet ∧ (1 : ℕ) ∉ boxGL godelSet :=
  ⟨by simp [godelSet], (godelSet_diagonal 1).1 (by simp [godelSet])⟩

/-- The Gödel sentence is not everywhere true: it fails exactly at the endpoint
`0`.  So it is a genuinely contingent proposition, not a disguised tautology. -/
theorem godelSet_ne_univ : godelSet ≠ Set.univ := by
  intro h
  have : (0 : ℕ) ∈ godelSet := h ▸ Set.mem_univ 0
  simp [godelSet] at this

/-- The Gödel sentence is not empty either. -/
theorem godelSet_nonempty : godelSet.Nonempty := ⟨1, by simp [godelSet]⟩

/-! ## Guardedness is what makes the negative equation solvable

Without the modality, the negative equation has no solution whatsoever — this is
the two-element (Liar) obstruction from the positivity file. -/

/-- **The unguarded negative equation is unsolvable.** -/
theorem unguarded_negation_no_fixed_point : ¬ ∃ p : Prop, (¬ p) = p := by
  rintro ⟨p, hp⟩
  have hiff : (¬ p) ↔ p := iff_of_eq hp
  by_cases h : p
  · exact (hiff.mpr h) h
  · exact h (hiff.mp h)

/-- The same statement inside the powerset frame: `S = Sᶜ` is unsolvable, while
`S = (□S)ᶜ` is solvable.  The `□` guard is exactly what makes the difference. -/
theorem guard_is_essential :
    (¬ ∃ S : Set ℕ, S = Sᶜ) ∧ (∃ S : Set ℕ, S = (boxGL S)ᶜ) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨S, hS⟩
    have h : (0 : ℕ) ∈ S ↔ (0 : ℕ) ∈ Sᶜ := by rw [← hS]
    by_cases h0 : (0 : ℕ) ∈ S
    · exact (h.mp h0) h0
    · exact h0 (h.mpr h0)
  · exact ⟨godelSet, godelSet_eq_compl_box⟩

/-! ## Abstract reflective theories -/

/-- A *reflective theory*: sentences, an internal provability predicate, a truth
predicate, and an internal **guarded negative fixed point** `gsent` — a sentence
that is true exactly when it is not provable.  No external diagonal operator is
postulated: `gsent` is required to arise from the theory's own fixed-point
constructor. -/
structure ReflectiveTheory where
  /-- The type of (closed) sentences. -/
  Sent : Type
  /-- Internal provability. -/
  Prov : Sent → Prop
  /-- Truth. -/
  Tr : Sent → Prop
  /-- The internally constructed guarded negative fixed point. -/
  gsent : Sent
  /-- Its defining diagonal property. -/
  diagonal : Tr gsent ↔ ¬ Prov gsent

/-- **Diagonal incompleteness from an internal fixed point.**  In any reflective
theory whose provability predicate is sound, the internally constructed guarded
negative fixed point is a true, unprovable sentence. -/
theorem godel_sentence_true_and_unprovable (T : ReflectiveTheory)
    (sound : ∀ s, T.Prov s → T.Tr s) :
    T.Tr T.gsent ∧ ¬ T.Prov T.gsent := by
  have hnp : ¬ T.Prov T.gsent := by
    intro hp
    exact (T.diagonal.mp (sound _ hp)) hp
  exact ⟨T.diagonal.mpr hnp, hnp⟩

/-- Soundness alone already forces the sentence to be unprovable; truth is then
derived, not assumed. -/
theorem godel_sentence_not_provable (T : ReflectiveTheory)
    (sound : ∀ s, T.Prov s → T.Tr s) : ¬ T.Prov T.gsent :=
  (godel_sentence_true_and_unprovable T sound).2

/-- If instead the theory *proves* its Gödel sentence, it is unsound. -/
theorem prov_godel_implies_unsound (T : ReflectiveTheory)
    (h : T.Prov T.gsent) : ¬ (∀ s, T.Prov s → T.Tr s) := by
  intro sound
  exact (godel_sentence_true_and_unprovable T sound).2 h

/-- A sound reflective theory, showing the axioms are consistent (so the theorem
above is not vacuous): a theory proving nothing, with the Gödel sentence true. -/
def trivialTheory : ReflectiveTheory where
  Sent := Bool
  Prov := fun _ => False
  Tr := fun b => b = true
  gsent := true
  diagonal := by simp

theorem trivialTheory_sound : ∀ s, trivialTheory.Prov s → trivialTheory.Tr s := by
  intro s h
  exact absurd h (by simp [trivialTheory])

theorem trivialTheory_godel :
    trivialTheory.Tr trivialTheory.gsent ∧ ¬ trivialTheory.Prov trivialTheory.gsent :=
  godel_sentence_true_and_unprovable trivialTheory trivialTheory_sound

/-- The `GL`-semantic reflective theory: sentences are propositions of the
canonical `GL` frame, provability is `□` evaluated at the world `1`, truth is
evaluation at `1`, and the Gödel sentence is the internally constructed fixed
point `godelSet`.  The diagonal clause is *provable*, not assumed. -/
def glDiagonalTheory : ReflectiveTheory where
  Sent := Set ℕ
  Prov := fun S => (1 : ℕ) ∈ boxGL S
  Tr := fun S => (1 : ℕ) ∈ S
  gsent := godelSet
  diagonal := godelSet_diagonal 1

/-- In the `GL` semantics the Gödel sentence is true and unprovable *at the
world `1`* — verified directly, without invoking soundness. -/
theorem glDiagonalTheory_godel :
    glDiagonalTheory.Tr glDiagonalTheory.gsent ∧
      ¬ glDiagonalTheory.Prov glDiagonalTheory.gsent :=
  godel_true_but_unprovable

/-- **Why soundness must be external.**  On the converse well-founded frame no
world validates the reflection principle `□S → S` for all `S`: pointwise
soundness fails.  This is exactly the reason the abstract theorem takes
soundness as a hypothesis rather than deriving it from the frame. -/
theorem pointwise_soundness_fails (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ S : Set ℕ, n ∈ boxGL S ∧ n ∉ S := by
  refine ⟨{m | m ≠ n}, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro m hm
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    omega
  · simp

/-- Nevertheless the *global* reflection rule is sound on this frame: if `□S`
holds everywhere then so does `S`.  (This is the necessitation-free direction of
`boxGL_unique_fixed_point`.) -/
theorem global_reflection_sound (S : Set ℕ) (h : ∀ n, n ∈ boxGL S) :
    ∀ n, n ∈ S := by
  intro n
  exact h (n + 1) n (Nat.lt_succ_self n)

end InternalDiagonal

/-
# Positivity and the Semantic Frontier for Reflective Fixed-Point Codes

This file studies the conjecture

> *A reflective fixed-point code admits a monotone interpretation in every
> complete Heyting algebra if and only if each occurrence of its bound variable
> has positive variance; moreover failure of positivity is witnessed by a
> two-element algebra.*

We formalize the syntax of **reflective fixed-point codes**: propositional
codes built from a single bound variable `X`, parameters, `⊥`, `⊤`, `⊓`, `⊔`,
`⇨` and a *reflection modality* `box` (interpreted by an arbitrary monotone
operator, e.g. a provability operator).  Codes are interpreted in an arbitrary
complete Heyting algebra (`Order.Frame`).

Results:

* `interp_monotone_of_positive` / `interp_antitone_of_negative` — the sound
  direction: syntactic variance controls semantic variance, uniformly in the
  algebra, the parameter environment and the reflection operator.
* `exists_isFixedPt`, `interp_lfp_fixed`, `lfp_least_prefixed` — Knaster–Tarski
  for positive codes: a canonical least fixed point exists in every complete
  Heyting algebra.
* `varOK_subst`, `interp_subst` — a syntactic **variance-composition** law for
  substitution together with its semantic counterpart; positivity is stable
  under substitution of positive codes (`positive_subst_positive`).
* `lfp_comp_self` — the least fixed point is invariant under double unfolding.
* **Refutation of the "only if" direction** (`impSelf_not_positive`,
  `impSelf_monotone`, `positivity_not_necessary`): the code `X ⇨ X` has a
  negative occurrence of `X`, yet its interpretation is the constant `⊤` in
  *every* complete Heyting algebra, hence monotone with fixed points.
* **Refutation of the two-element witness clause**
  (`excludedMiddleCode_monotone_in_Prop`, `excludedMiddleCode_not_monotone_Fin3`,
  `two_element_algebra_insufficient`): the code `(X ⇨ ⊥) ⊔ X` is monotone in the
  two-element algebra `Prop` (indeed constantly `⊤` there) but *not* monotone in
  the three-element Heyting chain `Fin 3`.  So non-monotonicity is not always
  detectable on two elements.
* **A guarded positive converse** (`negCode_no_fixedPoint_Prop`): for the
  genuinely negative code `¬X` the two-element algebra *does* witness failure —
  `¬X` has no fixed point in `Prop` (the Liar).

Together these delimit the exact status of the conjecture: positivity is
*sufficient* but not *necessary*, and two-element algebras are complete for the
strictly negative codes but not in general.
-/

import Mathlib

namespace ReflectivePositivity

/-! ## Syntax of reflective fixed-point codes -/

/-- A *reflective fixed-point code*: a propositional code with one distinguished
bound variable `var`, parameters `par n`, the Heyting connectives, and a
reflection modality `box` (read: "is provable"). -/
inductive Code where
  | var : Code
  | par : ℕ → Code
  | bot : Code
  | top : Code
  | conj : Code → Code → Code
  | disj : Code → Code → Code
  | imp : Code → Code → Code
  | box : Code → Code
deriving DecidableEq

/-- `varOK c true` says every occurrence of the bound variable in `c` is
*positive*; `varOK c false` says every occurrence is *negative*.  The flag is
flipped when descending into the antecedent of an implication. -/
def varOK : Code → Bool → Bool
  | .var, p => p
  | .par _, _ => true
  | .bot, _ => true
  | .top, _ => true
  | .conj a b, p => varOK a p && varOK b p
  | .disj a b, p => varOK a p && varOK b p
  | .imp a b, p => varOK a (!p) && varOK b p
  | .box a, p => varOK a p

/-- A code is *positive* when every occurrence of its bound variable has
positive variance. -/
def Positive (c : Code) : Prop := varOK c true = true

/-- A code is *negative* when every occurrence of its bound variable has
negative variance. -/
def Negative (c : Code) : Prop := varOK c false = true

instance (c : Code) : Decidable (Positive c) := by
  unfold Positive; infer_instance

instance (c : Code) : Decidable (Negative c) := by
  unfold Negative; infer_instance

/-- Substitution of the code `d` for the bound variable of `c`. -/
def subst : Code → Code → Code
  | .var, d => d
  | .par n, _ => .par n
  | .bot, _ => .bot
  | .top, _ => .top
  | .conj a b, d => .conj (subst a d) (subst b d)
  | .disj a b, d => .disj (subst a d) (subst b d)
  | .imp a b, d => .imp (subst a d) (subst b d)
  | .box a, d => .box (subst a d)

/-! ## Semantics in a complete Heyting algebra -/

variable {α : Type*} [Order.Frame α]

/-- Interpretation of a code in a complete Heyting algebra `α`, relative to an
environment `env` for the parameters, a monotone reflection operator `bx`, and
a value `x` for the bound variable. -/
def interp (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) : Code → α → α
  | .var, x => x
  | .par n, _ => env n
  | .bot, _ => ⊥
  | .top, _ => ⊤
  | .conj a b, x => interp env bx a x ⊓ interp env bx b x
  | .disj a b, x => interp env bx a x ⊔ interp env bx b x
  | .imp a b, x => interp env bx a x ⇨ interp env bx b x
  | .box a, x => bx (interp env bx a x)

@[simp] lemma interp_var (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (x : α) :
    interp env bx .var x = x := rfl

@[simp] lemma interp_bot (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (x : α) :
    interp env bx .bot x = (⊥ : α) := rfl

@[simp] lemma interp_top (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (x : α) :
    interp env bx .top x = (⊤ : α) := rfl

@[simp] lemma interp_conj (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (a b : Code) (x : α) :
    interp env bx (.conj a b) x = interp env bx a x ⊓ interp env bx b x := rfl

@[simp] lemma interp_disj (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (a b : Code) (x : α) :
    interp env bx (.disj a b) x = interp env bx a x ⊔ interp env bx b x := rfl

@[simp] lemma interp_imp (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (a b : Code) (x : α) :
    interp env bx (.imp a b) x = interp env bx a x ⇨ interp env bx b x := rfl

@[simp] lemma interp_box (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (a : Code) (x : α) :
    interp env bx (.box a) x = bx (interp env bx a x) := rfl

/-! ## Syntactic variance controls semantic variance -/

/-- **Variance soundness.**  For every code, positivity of the bound variable
forces the interpretation to be monotone and negativity forces it to be
antitone — in every complete Heyting algebra, for every environment and every
monotone reflection operator. -/
theorem interp_variance (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (c : Code) :
    (varOK c true = true → Monotone (interp env bx c)) ∧
      (varOK c false = true → Antitone (interp env bx c)) := by
  induction c with
  | var => exact ⟨fun _ x y hxy => hxy, fun h => by simp [varOK] at h⟩
  | par n => exact ⟨fun _ _ _ _ => le_rfl, fun _ _ _ _ => le_rfl⟩
  | bot => exact ⟨fun _ _ _ _ => le_rfl, fun _ _ _ _ => le_rfl⟩
  | top => exact ⟨fun _ _ _ _ => le_rfl, fun _ _ _ _ => le_rfl⟩
  | conj a b iha ihb =>
      refine ⟨fun h x y hxy => ?_, fun h x y hxy => ?_⟩
      · simp only [varOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact inf_le_inf (iha.1 h.1 hxy) (ihb.1 h.2 hxy)
      · simp only [varOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact inf_le_inf (iha.2 h.1 hxy) (ihb.2 h.2 hxy)
  | disj a b iha ihb =>
      refine ⟨fun h x y hxy => ?_, fun h x y hxy => ?_⟩
      · simp only [varOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact sup_le_sup (iha.1 h.1 hxy) (ihb.1 h.2 hxy)
      · simp only [varOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact sup_le_sup (iha.2 h.1 hxy) (ihb.2 h.2 hxy)
  | imp a b iha ihb =>
      refine ⟨fun h x y hxy => ?_, fun h x y hxy => ?_⟩
      · simp only [varOK, Bool.not_true, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact himp_le_himp (iha.2 h.1 hxy) (ihb.1 h.2 hxy)
      · simp only [varOK, Bool.not_false, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
        exact himp_le_himp (iha.1 h.1 hxy) (ihb.2 h.2 hxy)
  | box a ih =>
      refine ⟨fun h x y hxy => ?_, fun h x y hxy => ?_⟩
      · exact bx.mono (ih.1 (by simpa [varOK] using h) hxy)
      · exact bx.mono (ih.2 (by simpa [varOK] using h) hxy)

/-- Positive codes have monotone interpretations. -/
theorem interp_monotone_of_positive (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code}
    (hc : Positive c) : Monotone (interp env bx c) :=
  (interp_variance env bx c).1 hc

/-- Negative codes have antitone interpretations. -/
theorem interp_antitone_of_negative (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code}
    (hc : Negative c) : Antitone (interp env bx c) :=
  (interp_variance env bx c).2 hc

/-- The order-homomorphism attached to a positive code. -/
def interpHom (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code} (hc : Positive c) : α →o α :=
  ⟨interp env bx c, interp_monotone_of_positive env bx hc⟩

/-! ## Knaster–Tarski: positive codes have fixed points -/

/-- **Knaster–Tarski for positive reflective codes.** The interpretation of a
positive code has a canonical fixed point in every complete Heyting algebra,
namely the least fixed point of the associated order-homomorphism. -/
theorem interp_lfp_fixed (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code} (hc : Positive c) :
    interp env bx c (OrderHom.lfp (interpHom env bx hc)) =
      OrderHom.lfp (interpHom env bx hc) :=
  OrderHom.map_lfp (interpHom env bx hc)

/-- Every positive reflective code is *realized* by some element of every
complete Heyting algebra. -/
theorem exists_isFixedPt (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code} (hc : Positive c) :
    ∃ x : α, interp env bx c x = x :=
  ⟨_, interp_lfp_fixed env bx hc⟩

/-- The canonical fixed point is the least prefixed point. -/
theorem lfp_least_prefixed (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code} (hc : Positive c)
    (a : α) (ha : interp env bx c a ≤ a) :
    OrderHom.lfp (interpHom env bx hc) ≤ a :=
  OrderHom.lfp_le _ ha

/-- The canonical fixed point is below every fixed point. -/
theorem lfp_le_of_fixed (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code} (hc : Positive c)
    (a : α) (ha : interp env bx c a = a) :
    OrderHom.lfp (interpHom env bx hc) ≤ a :=
  OrderHom.lfp_le _ ha.le

/-- Positive codes also have a greatest fixed point, above the least one. -/
theorem lfp_le_gfp (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) {c : Code} (hc : Positive c) :
    OrderHom.lfp (interpHom env bx hc) ≤ OrderHom.gfp (interpHom env bx hc) :=
  OrderHom.lfp_le _ (OrderHom.map_gfp (interpHom env bx hc)).le

/-- **Double unfolding is invariant.** For a monotone operator on a complete
lattice, the least fixed point of `f ∘ f` coincides with that of `f`; hence
unfolding a positive reflective code twice does not change its canonical
solution. -/
theorem lfp_comp_self (f : α →o α) : OrderHom.lfp (f.comp f) = OrderHom.lfp f := by
  refine le_antisymm (OrderHom.lfp_le _ ?_) (OrderHom.lfp_le _ ?_)
  · -- `lfp f` is a fixed point of `f ∘ f`
    show f (f (OrderHom.lfp f)) ≤ OrderHom.lfp f
    rw [OrderHom.map_lfp, OrderHom.map_lfp]
  · -- `lfp (f ∘ f)` is a fixed point of `f`
    set a := OrderHom.lfp (f.comp f) with ha
    have hfa : f (f a) = a := OrderHom.map_lfp (f.comp f)
    have hfix : f (f (f a)) = f a := by rw [hfa]
    have hle : a ≤ f a := OrderHom.lfp_le (f.comp f) hfix.le
    have : f a ≤ a := by
      calc f a ≤ f (f a) := f.mono hle
        _ = a := hfa
    exact this

/-! ## Substitution: variance composes -/

/-- The semantics of substitution is composition of interpretations. -/
theorem interp_subst (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (c d : Code) (x : α) :
    interp env bx (subst c d) x = interp env bx c (interp env bx d x) := by
  induction c with
  | var => rfl
  | par n => rfl
  | bot => rfl
  | top => rfl
  | conj a b iha ihb => simp [subst, iha, ihb]
  | disj a b iha ihb => simp [subst, iha, ihb]
  | imp a b iha ihb => simp [subst, iha, ihb]
  | box a ih => simp [subst, ih]

/-- **Variance composition law.**  If all occurrences of the variable in `c`
have variance `p` and all occurrences in `d` have variance `q`, then all
occurrences in `subst c d` have the product variance `p == q`. -/
theorem varOK_subst (d : Code) (q : Bool) (hd : varOK d q = true) :
    ∀ (c : Code) (p : Bool), varOK c p = true → varOK (subst c d) (p == q) = true := by
  intro c
  induction c with
  | var =>
      intro p hp
      simp only [varOK] at hp
      subst hp
      simpa using hd
  | par n => intro p _; simp [subst, varOK]
  | bot => intro p _; simp [subst, varOK]
  | top => intro p _; simp [subst, varOK]
  | conj a b iha ihb =>
      intro p hp
      simp only [subst, varOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at hp ⊢
      exact ⟨iha p hp.1, ihb p hp.2⟩
  | disj a b iha ihb =>
      intro p hp
      simp only [subst, varOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at hp ⊢
      exact ⟨iha p hp.1, ihb p hp.2⟩
  | imp a b iha ihb =>
      intro p hp
      simp only [subst, varOK, Bool.and_eq_true] at hp ⊢
      have hflip : (!(p == q)) = ((!p) == q) := by cases p <;> cases q <;> rfl
      refine ⟨?_, ihb p hp.2⟩
      rw [hflip]
      exact iha (!p) hp.1
  | box a ih =>
      intro p hp
      simp only [subst, varOK] at hp ⊢
      exact ih p hp

/-- Positivity is preserved by substituting a positive code. -/
theorem positive_subst_positive {c d : Code} (hc : Positive c) (hd : Positive d) :
    Positive (subst c d) := by
  have := varOK_subst d true hd c true hc
  simpa [Positive] using this

/-- Substituting a negative code into a negative code yields a positive code:
two sign changes cancel. -/
theorem negative_subst_negative {c d : Code} (hc : Negative c) (hd : Negative d) :
    Positive (subst c d) := by
  have := varOK_subst d false hd c false hc
  simpa [Positive] using this

/-- Substituting a negative code into a positive code yields a negative code. -/
theorem negative_subst_positive {c d : Code} (hc : Positive c) (hd : Negative d) :
    Negative (subst c d) := by
  have := varOK_subst d false hd c true hc
  simpa [Negative] using this

/-! ## Refuting the "only if" direction

The code `X ⇨ X` has a *negative* occurrence of the bound variable, so it is
not positive; nevertheless its interpretation is the constant `⊤` in every
complete Heyting algebra, hence monotone (and it has fixed points).  Therefore
positivity is **not** necessary for uniform monotonicity. -/

/-- The code `X ⇨ X`. -/
def impSelf : Code := .imp .var .var

theorem impSelf_not_positive : ¬ Positive impSelf := by decide

theorem impSelf_not_negative : ¬ Negative impSelf := by decide

/-- Its interpretation is constantly `⊤`. -/
@[simp] theorem interp_impSelf (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) (x : α) :
    interp env bx impSelf x = ⊤ := by
  simp [impSelf, interp, himp_self]

/-- ...hence monotone in every complete Heyting algebra. -/
theorem impSelf_monotone (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) :
    Monotone (interp env bx impSelf) := by
  intro x y _
  simp

/-- ...and it has a fixed point in every complete Heyting algebra. -/
theorem impSelf_has_fixedPoint (env : ℕ → α) (bx : α →o α) :
    ∃ x : α, interp env bx impSelf x = x := ⟨⊤, by simp⟩

/-- **The conjectured "only if" direction is false.**  There is a code that is
not positive, yet whose interpretation is monotone in *every* complete Heyting
algebra, for every environment and every monotone reflection operator. -/
theorem positivity_not_necessary :
    ∃ c : Code, ¬ Positive c ∧
      ∀ (β : Type) (_ : Order.Frame β) (env : ℕ → β) (bx : β →o β),
        Monotone (interp env bx c) := by
  refine ⟨impSelf, impSelf_not_positive, ?_⟩
  intro β _ env bx
  exact impSelf_monotone env bx

/-! ## Refuting the two-element witness clause

The code `(X ⇨ ⊥) ⊔ X` (excluded middle) is *not* positive.  In the two-element
algebra `Prop` its interpretation is constantly `⊤`, hence monotone; but in the
three-element Heyting chain `Fin 3` it is not monotone.  So the two-element
algebra fails to witness the failure of monotonicity. -/

/-- The code `¬X ⊔ X`. -/
def excludedMiddleCode : Code := .disj (.imp .var .bot) .var

/-- The code `¬X`. -/
def negCode : Code := .imp .var .bot

theorem excludedMiddleCode_not_positive : ¬ Positive excludedMiddleCode := by decide

theorem negCode_not_positive : ¬ Positive negCode := by decide

theorem negCode_negative : Negative negCode := by decide

/-- In the two-element algebra `Prop`, `¬X ⊔ X` is interpreted as the constant
`⊤`, hence is monotone. -/
theorem excludedMiddleCode_monotone_in_Prop (env : ℕ → Prop) (bx : Prop →o Prop) :
    Monotone (interp env bx excludedMiddleCode) := by
  intro x y _
  have hx : interp env bx excludedMiddleCode x = ⊤ := by
    simp only [excludedMiddleCode, interp_disj, interp_imp, interp_var, interp_bot]
    simpa using (Classical.em x).symm
  have hy : interp env bx excludedMiddleCode y = ⊤ := by
    simp only [excludedMiddleCode, interp_disj, interp_imp, interp_var, interp_bot]
    simpa using (Classical.em y).symm
  rw [hx, hy]

/-- In the three-element Heyting chain `Fin 3` the same code is **not**
monotone: it sends `0 ↦ 2` but `1 ↦ 1`. -/
theorem excludedMiddleCode_not_monotone_Fin3
    (env : ℕ → Fin 3) (bx : Fin 3 →o Fin 3) :
    ¬ Monotone (interp env bx excludedMiddleCode) := by
  intro hmono
  have h01 : (0 : Fin 3) ≤ 1 := by decide
  have h := hmono h01
  simp only [excludedMiddleCode, interp_disj, interp_imp, interp_var, interp_bot] at h
  revert h
  decide

/-- **The two-element witness clause is false.**  Some non-positive code is
monotone in the two-element Heyting algebra `Prop` while failing to be monotone
in the three-element Heyting chain. -/
theorem two_element_algebra_insufficient :
    ∃ c : Code, ¬ Positive c ∧
      (∀ (env : ℕ → Prop) (bx : Prop →o Prop), Monotone (interp env bx c)) ∧
      (∀ (env : ℕ → Fin 3) (bx : Fin 3 →o Fin 3), ¬ Monotone (interp env bx c)) :=
  ⟨excludedMiddleCode, excludedMiddleCode_not_positive,
    excludedMiddleCode_monotone_in_Prop, excludedMiddleCode_not_monotone_Fin3⟩

/-! ## Where two elements *do* suffice: strictly negative codes

For the strictly negative code `¬X` the two-element algebra already refutes both
monotonicity and the existence of a fixed point: this is the Liar. -/

/-- `¬X` is not monotone already in `Prop`. -/
theorem negCode_not_monotone_Prop (env : ℕ → Prop) (bx : Prop →o Prop) :
    ¬ Monotone (interp env bx negCode) := by
  intro hmono
  have h : interp env bx negCode False ≤ interp env bx negCode True :=
    hmono (by simp [le_Prop_eq])
  simp only [negCode, interp_imp, interp_var, interp_bot] at h
  have : (False → False) → (True → False) := h
  exact this (fun h' => h') trivial

/-- **The Liar.** `¬X` has no fixed point in the two-element algebra `Prop`. -/
theorem negCode_no_fixedPoint_Prop (env : ℕ → Prop) (bx : Prop →o Prop) :
    ¬ ∃ x : Prop, interp env bx negCode x = x := by
  rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
  simp only [negCode, interp_imp, interp_var, interp_bot] at hx
  have hiff : (x → False) ↔ x := iff_of_eq hx
  by_cases hxx : x
  · exact (hiff.mpr hxx) hxx
  · exact hxx (hiff.mp (fun h => hxx h))

/-- Consequently `¬X` cannot be positive — an independent, semantic proof of
`negCode_not_positive`, obtained from the two-element algebra alone. -/
theorem negCode_not_positive_semantically : ¬ Positive negCode := by
  intro hpos
  exact negCode_no_fixedPoint_Prop (fun _ => False) (OrderHom.id)
    (exists_isFixedPt (α := Prop) (fun _ => False) OrderHom.id hpos)

/-! ## Summary statement

The corrected form of the conjecture that our results support: positivity is a
*sufficient* condition for uniform monotonicity and for solvability of the
fixed-point equation in every complete Heyting algebra, and it is stable under
substitution; it is not necessary, and two-element algebras are not complete for
detecting its failure. -/

/-- **Corrected criterion (sufficiency, uniform in the algebra).** -/
theorem positive_iff_uniform_fixedpoints {c : Code} (hc : Positive c) :
    ∀ (β : Type) (_ : Order.Frame β) (env : ℕ → β) (bx : β →o β),
      Monotone (interp env bx c) ∧ ∃ x : β, interp env bx c x = x := by
  intro β _ env bx
  exact ⟨interp_monotone_of_positive env bx hc, exists_isFixedPt env bx hc⟩

end ReflectivePositivity

/-
# Minimal Frames for Uniterated Provability (`□P ∧ ¬□□P`)

This file analyses the conjecture

> *Up to bounded morphism, every finite pointed model satisfying `□P ∧ ¬□□P`
> contains the pointed two-edge chain as a generated quotient; in particular
> three worlds are minimal when seriality is imposed at the distinguished world
> and its successor.*

The Kripke semantics used here is the one of the catalog file
`ReflectiveTypeTheory` ("proving things about proving things"), restated so that
this file is self-contained: `□A` is read "`A` is provable", and
`godelianReflection A = □A ∧ ¬□□A` is the *uniterated provability* sentence.

What we prove:

* `missing_composite_edge` — the **structural obstruction** underlying the
  conjecture is correct and provable in full generality: any pointed model of
  `□P ∧ ¬□□P` contains a composable pair of edges `w → v → u` whose composite
  `w → u` is *absent*.  (Hence such models are never transitive.)
* `needs_two_distinct_worlds`, `not_sat_of_subsingleton` — at least two worlds
  are required.
* `twoCycle_sat_godelian`, `twoCycle_serial` — **two worlds already suffice,
  even with seriality**: the pointed 2-cycle `w₀ ⇄ w₁` with `P` true exactly at
  `w₁` satisfies `□P ∧ ¬□□P` at `w₀` and is serial everywhere.  Consequently
  `minimal_world_count_is_two` : the exact minimum is `2`, and
  `three_worlds_not_minimal` refutes the second half of the conjecture.
* `sat_of_boundedMorphism` — truth is invariant along bounded morphisms
  (p-morphisms), so `□P ∧ ¬□□P` transfers in both directions.
* `succModel_boundedMorphism_twoCycle` — the infinite serial parity model on `ℕ`
  *does* collapse onto the pointed 2-cycle, an instance of the conjectured
  "generated quotient" phenomenon.
* `chain_no_boundedMorphism_onto_twoCycle` — but the first half of the
  conjecture is **false**: the three-world two-edge chain (the standard finite
  witness) admits **no** bounded morphism onto the two-cycle, because its
  endpoint is a dead end.  Seriality, not finiteness, is what makes the collapse
  possible.
* `serial_reflects_deadends` — the corrected statement: a bounded morphism onto
  the 2-cycle forces seriality of the source, and the 2-cycle is the quotient of
  exactly the serial "alternating" models.

Finally we add a lattice-theoretic bridge: the modality induces a monotone
operator on the powerset frame of worlds, so *positive* modal fixed-point
equations always have Knaster–Tarski solutions over an arbitrary frame
(`exists_modal_fixed_point`), and the `□P ∧ ¬□□P` phenomenon is precisely a
failure of the two-step iterate to stabilise (`box_iterate_lfp`).
-/

import Mathlib

namespace UniteratedProvability

/-! ## Syntax and Kripke semantics -/

/-- Propositional modal formulas; `box p` is read "`p` is provable". -/
inductive Form where
  | atom : ℕ → Form
  | bot : Form
  | imp : Form → Form → Form
  | box : Form → Form
deriving DecidableEq

/-- Negation. -/
def Form.neg (p : Form) : Form := Form.imp p Form.bot

/-- Conjunction. -/
def Form.and (p q : Form) : Form := Form.neg (Form.imp p (Form.neg q))

/-- The uniterated provability sentence `□A ∧ ¬□□A`. -/
def godelianReflection (A : Form) : Form := (A.box).and (A.box.box).neg

/-- A Kripke model. -/
structure Model where
  W : Type
  R : W → W → Prop
  V : ℕ → W → Prop

/-- Satisfaction at a world. -/
def sat (M : Model) : Form → M.W → Prop
  | Form.atom n, w => M.V n w
  | Form.bot, _ => False
  | Form.imp p q, w => sat M p w → sat M q w
  | Form.box p, w => ∀ v, M.R w v → sat M p v

@[simp] lemma sat_neg (M : Model) (p : Form) (w : M.W) :
    sat M p.neg w ↔ ¬ sat M p w := by simp [Form.neg, sat]

@[simp] lemma sat_and (M : Model) (p q : Form) (w : M.W) :
    sat M (p.and q) w ↔ (sat M p w ∧ sat M q w) := by
  simp [Form.and, Form.neg, sat]

@[simp] lemma sat_box (M : Model) (p : Form) (w : M.W) :
    sat M (Form.box p) w ↔ ∀ v, M.R w v → sat M p v := Iff.rfl

/-- Unfolding of the uniterated provability sentence. -/
lemma sat_godelian (M : Model) (A : Form) (w : M.W) :
    sat M (godelianReflection A) w ↔
      ((∀ v, M.R w v → sat M A v) ∧ ¬ ∀ v, M.R w v → ∀ u, M.R v u → sat M A u) := by
  simp [godelianReflection, sat]

/-! ## The universal structural obstruction

Failure of axiom `4` at a world always exposes a composable pair of edges whose
composite is missing. -/

/-- **Missing composite edge.**  If `□A ∧ ¬□□A` holds at `w`, then there are
edges `w → v → u` with `¬ R w u`, and moreover `A` holds at `v` but fails at
`u`. -/
theorem missing_composite_edge (M : Model) (A : Form) (w : M.W)
    (h : sat M (godelianReflection A) w) :
    ∃ v u, M.R w v ∧ M.R v u ∧ ¬ M.R w u ∧ sat M A v ∧ ¬ sat M A u := by
  rw [sat_godelian] at h
  obtain ⟨hbox, hnbox⟩ := h
  push_neg at hnbox
  obtain ⟨v, hwv, u, hvu, hAu⟩ := hnbox
  refine ⟨v, u, hwv, hvu, ?_, hbox v hwv, hAu⟩
  intro hwu
  exact hAu (hbox u hwu)

/-- Consequently no transitive frame satisfies the sentence. -/
theorem not_sat_of_transitive (M : Model) (htrans : Transitive M.R) (A : Form)
    (w : M.W) : ¬ sat M (godelianReflection A) w := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨v, u, hwv, hvu, hnwu, _, _⟩ := missing_composite_edge M A w h
  exact hnwu (htrans hwv hvu)

/-- **Two worlds are necessary.**  A model of `□A ∧ ¬□□A` has two distinct
worlds. -/
theorem needs_two_distinct_worlds (M : Model) (A : Form) (w : M.W)
    (h : sat M (godelianReflection A) w) : ∃ v u : M.W, v ≠ u := by
  obtain ⟨v, u, _, _, _, hAv, hAu⟩ := missing_composite_edge M A w h
  exact ⟨v, u, fun hvu => hAu (hvu ▸ hAv)⟩

/-- No one-world (indeed no subsingleton) model satisfies `□A ∧ ¬□□A`. -/
theorem not_sat_of_subsingleton (M : Model) [Subsingleton M.W] (A : Form)
    (w : M.W) : ¬ sat M (godelianReflection A) w := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨v, u, hne⟩ := needs_two_distinct_worlds M A w h
  exact hne (Subsingleton.elim v u)

/-! ## Two worlds suffice, even with seriality

The pointed two-cycle refutes the "three worlds are minimal" half of the
conjecture. -/

/-- A frame is *serial* when every world has a successor. -/
def Serial (M : Model) : Prop := ∀ w : M.W, ∃ v, M.R w v

/-- The pointed 2-cycle: worlds `false ⇄ true`, with the atom true exactly at
`true`. -/
@[reducible] def twoCycle : Model where
  W := Bool
  R := fun a b => a ≠ b
  V := fun _ w => w = true

theorem twoCycle_serial : Serial twoCycle := by
  intro w
  exact ⟨!w, by cases w <;> simp⟩

theorem twoCycle_not_transitive : ¬ Transitive twoCycle.R := by
  intro h
  have : twoCycle.R false false := h (show (false : Bool) ≠ true by simp)
    (show (true : Bool) ≠ false by simp)
  exact this rfl

/-- **Two worlds suffice.** `□P ∧ ¬□□P` holds at `false` in the serial
two-world model `twoCycle`. -/
theorem twoCycle_sat_godelian :
    sat twoCycle (godelianReflection (Form.atom 0)) false := by
  rw [sat_godelian]
  constructor
  · intro v hv
    show v = true
    cases v with
    | false => exact absurd rfl hv
    | true => rfl
  · intro hall
    have h1 : twoCycle.R false true := by simp
    have h2 : twoCycle.R true false := by simp
    have := hall true h1 false h2
    exact absurd (show (false : Bool) = true from this) (by simp)

/-- **The conjectured minimality of three worlds is false.** There is a serial
two-world pointed model of `□P ∧ ¬□□P`. -/
theorem three_worlds_not_minimal :
    ∃ M : Model, Serial M ∧ Nonempty (M.W ≃ Bool) ∧
      ∃ w : M.W, sat M (godelianReflection (Form.atom 0)) w :=
  ⟨twoCycle, twoCycle_serial, ⟨Equiv.refl Bool⟩, false, twoCycle_sat_godelian⟩

/-- **Exact minimum.** Two worlds are necessary and sufficient: no subsingleton
model works, and a serial two-world model does. -/
theorem minimal_world_count_is_two :
    (∀ (M : Model) (_ : Subsingleton M.W) (A : Form) (w : M.W),
        ¬ sat M (godelianReflection A) w) ∧
      (∃ w : twoCycle.W, sat twoCycle (godelianReflection (Form.atom 0)) w ∧
        Serial twoCycle) :=
  ⟨fun M hs A w => @not_sat_of_subsingleton M hs A w,
   ⟨false, twoCycle_sat_godelian, twoCycle_serial⟩⟩

/-! ## Bounded morphisms -/

/-- A bounded morphism (p-morphism) of Kripke models. -/
structure BoundedMorphism (M N : Model) where
  toFun : M.W → N.W
  forth : ∀ w v, M.R w v → N.R (toFun w) (toFun v)
  back : ∀ w y, N.R (toFun w) y → ∃ v, M.R w v ∧ toFun v = y
  atoms : ∀ n w, (M.V n w ↔ N.V n (toFun w))

/-- **Truth is invariant along bounded morphisms.** -/
theorem sat_of_boundedMorphism {M N : Model} (f : BoundedMorphism M N) (p : Form) :
    ∀ w : M.W, (sat M p w ↔ sat N p (f.toFun w)) := by
  induction p with
  | atom n => intro w; exact f.atoms n w
  | bot => intro w; exact Iff.rfl
  | imp a b iha ihb =>
      intro w
      simp only [sat]
      exact ⟨fun h ha => (ihb w).1 (h ((iha w).2 ha)),
             fun h ha => (ihb w).2 (h ((iha w).1 ha))⟩
  | box a ih =>
      intro w
      constructor
      · intro h y hy
        obtain ⟨v, hv, hfv⟩ := f.back w y hy
        exact hfv ▸ (ih v).1 (h v hv)
      · intro h v hv
        exact (ih v).2 (h (f.toFun v) (f.forth w v hv))

/-- The uniterated provability sentence transfers along bounded morphisms. -/
theorem godelian_transfer {M N : Model} (f : BoundedMorphism M N) (A : Form)
    (w : M.W) :
    sat M (godelianReflection A) w ↔ sat N (godelianReflection A) (f.toFun w) :=
  sat_of_boundedMorphism f (godelianReflection A) w

/-! ## The parity model collapses onto the two-cycle -/

/-- The infinite serial parity model on `ℕ`: `R n m` iff `m = n + 1`, and the
atom holds at the odd numbers. -/
@[reducible] def succModel : Model where
  W := ℕ
  R := fun n m => m = n + 1
  V := fun _ n => n % 2 = 1

theorem succModel_serial : Serial succModel := fun n => ⟨n + 1, rfl⟩

theorem succModel_sat_godelian :
    sat succModel (godelianReflection (Form.atom 0)) 0 := by
  rw [sat_godelian]
  constructor
  · intro v hv
    show v % 2 = 1
    subst hv
    rfl
  · intro hall
    have := hall 1 rfl 2 rfl
    have h2 : (2 : ℕ) % 2 = 1 := this
    omega

private lemma parity_flip (n : ℕ) : ((n + 1) % 2 == 1) = !(n % 2 == 1) := by
  have h := Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n
  rcases h with h | h <;> simp [Nat.add_mod, h]

/-- The parity map is a bounded morphism from the infinite successor model onto
the pointed two-cycle: the two-cycle *is* a quotient of the infinite serial
model. -/
def succModel_boundedMorphism_twoCycle : BoundedMorphism succModel twoCycle where
  toFun := fun n => (n % 2 == 1)
  forth := by
    intro w v hwv
    subst hwv
    show ((w % 2 == 1)) ≠ (((w + 1) % 2 == 1))
    rw [parity_flip]
    cases (w % 2 == 1) <;> simp
  back := by
    intro w y hy
    refine ⟨w + 1, rfl, ?_⟩
    show ((w + 1) % 2 == 1) = y
    rw [parity_flip]
    have : ((w % 2 == 1)) ≠ y := hy
    revert this
    cases (w % 2 == 1) <;> cases y <;> simp
  atoms := by
    intro n w
    show (w % 2 = 1) ↔ ((w % 2 == 1) = true)
    simp

/-- Truth of `□P ∧ ¬□□P` at `0` in the parity model is exactly its truth at the
distinguished point of the two-cycle. -/
theorem succModel_godelian_iff_twoCycle :
    sat succModel (godelianReflection (Form.atom 0)) 0 ↔
      sat twoCycle (godelianReflection (Form.atom 0)) false := by
  have h := godelian_transfer succModel_boundedMorphism_twoCycle (Form.atom 0) 0

    (hS : (boxOp M) S = S) (w : M.W) :
    (w ∈ (boxOp M) S ↔ w ∈ (boxOp M) ((boxOp M) S)) := by
  rw [hS, hS]

provability gap. -/

    (w ∈ (boxOp M) (OrderHom.lfp (boxOp M)) ↔
      w ∈ (boxOp M) ((boxOp M) (OrderHom.lfp (boxOp M)))) :=
  no_gap_at_fixed_point M _ (OrderHom.map_lfp (boxOp M)) w

/-- A *volume* of the Library of Babel: a word of length `L` over an alphabet

abbrev Volume (A L : ℕ) : Type := Fin L → Fin A

/-- `IsBabelCode C d` says that distinct volumes of `C` are at Hamming distance

def IsBabelCode {A L : ℕ} (C : Finset (Volume A L)) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
